title: Ribollita Tuscan Twice Boiled Soup

seo.title: Authentic Tuscan Ribollita Recipe - Hearty Italian Soup
seo.metaDescription: Discover our authentic Tuscan Ribollita recipe! This hearty, twice-boiled Italian bread and vegetable soup is perfect for a comforting meal. Easy step-by-step guide.

description: Ribollita is a quintessential Tuscan peasant soup, renowned for its hearty and comforting nature. This "twice-boiled" delight traditionally reuses leftover bread and vegetable minestrone, transforming humble ingredients into a rich, flavorful meal. It is a nourishing dish that embodies the true spirit of cucina povera, perfect for a warming and satisfying experience.

ingredients.item: Black kale (cavolo nero) or savoy cabbage

ingredients.notes: rinsed and drained (reserve some whole, mash some)

instructions.title: Prepare the Soffritto
instructions.text: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté gently for about 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent, being careful not to brown them.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics and Tomatoes
instructions.text: Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add the crushed tomatoes, rosemary, and thyme. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Simmer the Vegetables and Beans
instructions.text: Add the chopped black kale or savoy cabbage to the pot. Pour in the vegetable broth. Add one can of rinsed cannellini beans whole, and mash the second can of beans roughly before adding them to the pot. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for at least 20-25 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

instructions.title: Assemble the Ribollita Layers
instructions.text: Remove the rosemary and thyme sprigs. In an oven-safe casserole dish or back in the same pot (if large enough), arrange a layer of stale bread slices at the bottom. Ladle a generous amount of the hot vegetable and bean soup over the bread, ensuring it is well-soaked.

instructions.title: The "Twice-Boiled" Process
instructions.text: Continue layering bread and soup until all ingredients are used, finishing with a layer of soup. Gently press down to ensure the bread is submerged. Let the soup rest for at least 30 minutes, or ideally for a few hours (or even overnight in the refrigerator) to allow the bread to fully absorb the liquid and thicken the soup. This is the "twice-boiled" aspect - letting it sit and then reheating.

instructions.title: Reheat and Serve
instructions.text: Before serving, gently reheat the Ribollita on the stovetop over low heat or in a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) for 20-30 minutes, until heated through and bubbling gently. The soup should be thick and creamy. Serve hot, drizzled with a good quality extra virgin olive oil and optionally garnished with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

tips: For an authentic Tuscan touch, use unsalted bread (pane toscano) which is traditionally used in Ribollita and other Tuscan dishes. Stale bread is crucial for the soup's texture.

Cavolo Nero (black kale) is the traditional green for Ribollita, offering a slightly bitter and robust flavor. If unavailable, savoy cabbage or even regular kale can be used, though the flavor profile will differ slightly.
Ribollita famously tastes even better the next day! Prepare it ahead of time and allow the flavors to deepen overnight. When reheating, add a splash of broth or water if it's too thick.
